title: Browser evaluator class-group host
objective: Install the production class-group Wasm reactor lazily inside the Sage evaluator worker as a synchronous coarse Python runtime boundary, with exact session lifecycle, cancellation, memory bounds, and browser-engine qualification

oracles: Native service receipts, detached Python replay, and Chromium/Firefox/WebKit exact parity

handoff.summary: Preloads and receipt-authenticates the production class-group reactor directly inside the existing evaluator worker, exposes only synchronous __sagejs_host__.call("classGroup", [operation, request]), validates and unboxes the canonical service envelope, preserves typed error receipts, binds open results to the artifact SHA-256, tracks decimal-string generation/handle sessions, closes resident sessions on evaluator teardown, and enforces the 4096-page/256 MiB maximum. Focused Node host tests and real-artifact Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit tests pass.
risks: The lane depends on class-group-product-service retaining the canonical service-request-v1/service-response-v1 ABI and decimal-string generation/handle fields.
Cancellation during a synchronous Rust call remains evaluator-worker termination by design; the reactor has no resumable step ABI.

The full pnpm build and test:changed matrix is blocked in this worktree by an unrelated stale numerical production-manifest toolchain identity; focused evaluator and all three browser-engine tests pass.
next_steps: Integrate after class-group-product-service and class-group-wasm-product, then rebuild flint-wasm so the evaluator and reactor receipt are emitted in one production manifest.
Have the runtime-host lane delegate runtime.class_group_backend().call(op, request) to __sagejs_host__.call("classGroup", [op, request]).
Run the portable/native/SEA release matrix from the integrated clean build.
